readme: Reviewed, legitimate coverage gaps: the store carries the item but it genuinely cannot be priced like-for-like, so audit-coverage-gaps must not keep crying about it. Every entry states WHY, quoting the price_text/size_text the ENGINE actually saw. Do not add an entry to silence a gap you have not diagnosed - the detector exists to catch a store silently vanishing from an item it sells.

allow.why: UNPRICEABLE (UNIT-MISMATCH, reviewed 2026-07-28): the commodity is priced per EACH and Hy-Vee lists these by pack weight with no sandwich count. Engine saw price_text=[$7.49] size_text=[18 oz] for "Hy-Vee Sausage, Egg, & Cheese Muffin Breakfast Sandwiches" - deriving a count from ounces would be inventing one. Not a rule bug. NOTE: the same unit mismatch drops most of this commodity at most stores (Baker's prices only its 1 ct / 2 pk items); if Brad wants real coverage here the fix is to reprice breakfast-sandwiches per OZ, which is a commodity-definition call, not a triage call.
